metadata.title: Why Great Content Doesn't Always Perform?
metadata.audience: Students, creators and fellows publishing content who see strong posts underperform
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: Hawaiian (one word). Namaste/Hola/Hej/Ciao/Bonjour/Olá already used in this series. Chip @Shubh & @HumanitariansAI on every Claude page (B00 beginning, B05 middle, B11 + B12 end) and the outro.
metadata.note: ai-explainer, Plain register. New reel (not a variation): why strong content underperforms — audience fit, distribution, timing, format, platform algorithms and paid amplification, plus a diagnose beat where the content itself is the problem. No statistics, no platform-specific weights; every chart is illustrative with no numeric axis. Reel-local C3 scenes in runtime/remotion/src/scenes/ContentPerformance.tsx (+ ContentPerformance916.tsx). Never publishes.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude UI first; the ask lands answered. Chip @Shubh & @HumanitariansAI (beginning).
beats.narration_text: Aloha! I've watched really good posts get almost no views. So I asked Claude: why doesn't great content always perform?

props.command: I made a post I'm proud of, and it barely got any views. Why doesn't great content always perform? Break down everything besides quality that decides reach.
output: quality gets a post into the game
fit, distribution and timing decide who sees it
format, algorithms and paid reach decide how far it goes

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — hesitant writer. Misconception: great content ALWAYS FINDS its audience → it STILL HAS TO REACH its audience. Narration opens 'Hi, I'm Shubh…' per the brief.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Shubh, and this video is about why great content doesn't always perform. Quality is only the start. Audience fit, distribution, timing, format, algorithms and paid reach decide who actually sees it.

show.event: types 'Great content always finds its audience.'
'always' and 'finds' turn terracotta, backspace, become 'still' / 'has to reach'

props.text:
Great content
always finds

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the overview accumulates token by token, so the 50% sample is mid-typing; the corrected three-line overview (fontSize 250) fills the safe area from ~65% of the beat onward (verified at 85%).

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK FIRST — performance as a chain of seven links; each lights on its spoken name; at 'break one link' the timing link cracks (accent) and the reach flow stops there.
beats.narration_text: Think of performance as a chain. Quality is the first link. Then audience fit, distribution, timing, format, the algorithm, and paid reach. Break one link, and even a great post stalls.

show.event: fit → distribution → timing → format → algorithm → paid light in spoken order
timing link cracks (accent); reach flow stops at the break

beats.role_note: Factor 1 — audience fit: one budgeting guide shown to two rooms; the joke-scrolling room stays pale (skips), the students' room fills and saves (accent border).
beats.narration_text: Start with fit. Here's the same guide to budgeting in two rooms. A feed scrolling for jokes skips right past it. Students planning their first budget save it and share it. The post didn't change. The room did.

show.event: right room: dots fill, save marks, accent border

beats.role_note: Factor 2 — distribution: publish lights only part of the follower grid; three after-publish paths (newsletter, community, creator partner) each light a new cluster.
beats.narration_text: Next, distribution. Publishing only reaches some of your followers. Distribution is what you do after: send it to your newsletter, share it in a community, and team up with a creator whose audience fits.

show.event: part of the follower grid lights

beats.role_note: ASK→RESULT micro-beat, mid-reel Claude page (chip @Shubh & @HumanitariansAI, middle). Command pre-typed; output lines are METHOD, not invented results.
beats.narration_text: Timing and format are easier to test than to guess. So I asked Claude to help me read my own numbers.

show.event: composer with the ask already typed

props.command: Here are my last twenty posts with the day, time, format, views and saves. Which time slots and formats get the most saves? Suggest one test for next week.
output: group posts by time slot and by format
compare saves and shares, not just views
change one thing per test, keep the rest the same

beats.role_note: RESULT of B05 — factor 3, timing: an illustrative 24-hour audience curve; the same post dropped at 3 AM gets a small early-reaction bar; dropped at the evening peak, a big one that pushes 'shown to more people' (accent).
beats.narration_text: Timing is about when your audience is actually there. Post while they sleep, and the first hour stays quiet. Post when they're scrolling, and early reactions tell the platform to show it to more people.

show.event: post at 3 AM; tiny first-hour bar
same post at the evening peak; first-hour bar grows

beats.role_note: Factor 4 — format: two phones; a wall of text on a video-first feed is scrolled past; the same idea as a short vertical video with the point in the first seconds gets watched (accent hook segment).
beats.narration_text: Format is how the idea arrives. A wall of text on a video-first feed gets scrolled past. The same idea as a short vertical video, with the point in the first seconds, gets watched.

show.event: first-seconds hook segment (accent) on the progress bar

beats.role_note: Factor 5 — algorithm: a post shown to a small ring; four signal chips land (watch time, saves, shares, comments); strong signals widen the ring twice (accent loop arrow); weak-signal branch stops. Caption: simplified.
beats.narration_text: Then the algorithm. Many platforms show a post to a small group first, then read the signals: watch time, saves, shares, comments. Strong signals earn a bigger audience, and the loop repeats. Weak signals, and it stops.

show.event: signal chips land in spoken order
ring widens, then widens again (accent loop)

beats.role_note: Factor 6 — paid reach: two boosted lanes; wrong audience → views bar tall, results bar flat; right audience → both grow (accent on the right-audience results bar). No numbers.
beats.narration_text: Paid reach buys attention, not fit. Boost a post to the wrong audience, and you pay for views that never become follows or sales. Boost it to the right audience, and it multiplies what already works.

show.event: wrong-audience lane: views rise, results flat
right-audience lane: views and results rise (accent)

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — sometimes the content IS the problem: three questions in order (seen? stopped? acted?); each 'no' routes to its fix; the last fix, 'rework the content', takes the accent.
beats.narration_text: But be honest. Sometimes the content is the problem. Ask three questions. Did the right people see it? If not, fix fit and distribution. Did they stop? If not, fix format and the hook. Did they act? If not, rework the content itself.

beats.role_note: Verdict artifact page. Chip @Shubh & @HumanitariansAI via brandLabel (end).
beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Quality gets you in. Fit, distribution and timing decide who sees it. Format and the algorithm decide if they stay. Paid reach amplifies what already fits.

props.artifactTitle: Why Great Content Stalls — one page
props.artifactHeading: Quality is one link in the chain
artifactLines: Fit: the right post for the right room.
Distribution + timing: reach people when they're there.
Format + algorithm: hook fast, earn the signals.
Paid reach amplifies fit — it can't create it.
Still stuck? Ask: seen? stopped? acted?

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — prompt read aloud verbatim, then discussed. Chip @Shubh & @HumanitariansAI (end).
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Here's a post that underperformed, with who it was for, where and when I posted it, and its results. Using fit, distribution, timing, format, the algorithm and paid reach, tell me the most likely weak link, and one test to fix it. Asking for one test matters. It stops you changing everything at once, so you learn what actually worked.
